text:
maria: heads up — I noticed a latency regression in paged attention on master vs release-2026-03. small-ish change but shows up at seq=1024 + batch>=8 :grimacing:
jon: repro details? numbers, perf profile?
kevin: repro script: run ./bench/paged_attn_bench --seq 1024 --batch 8 --iters 200 on p4d. master -> p95 ~ 220ms, release -> 185ms. consistent across runs.
eva: ack. any flamegraphs or perf top?
maria: uploaded a flame snapshot to the perf bucket: gs://redwood-perf/paged-attn/2419998888/flame.svg
kevin: quick callout from perf top: ~42% time in kv_page_walk(), ~18% in flash_attn_copy(), rest in kernel launches. also large number of small allocations visible.
dana: small allocations for block table entries? we changed block-table lifecycle in that recent allocator refactor. might be fragmentation + more page faults. :thinking_face:
kevin: exact diff: allocator moved from per-shard fixed slab -> shard-adaptive slab with hotset reservations. heuristics use LRU aging to promote. new path introduces more frequent free/alloc churn under bursty long-context workloads.
jon: can you paste the allocator config used for the repro?
maria: sure:
```yaml
pager:
  alloc_strategy: shard-adaptive
  slab_size_mb: 64
  hot_reserve_pct: 12
  max_pages_per_shard: 8192
  ageing_window_ms: 250
```
kevin: curious thing — when I force alloc_strategy: small-slab-fixed the perf comes back to ~190ms. so difference narrow but real.
eva: hypothesis: churn causing extra KV cache pagewalks which in turn defeats the kernel fastpath (flashv2) and forces a fallback kernel that copies large KV blocks. we saw similar behaviour in earlier paged-attn experiments.
dana: can we test a kernel-selection guard: prefer flashv2 only if contiguous_kv_ratio > 0.8 and page_faults/sec < 50? quick patch might prove the point.
kevin: patched a local build to short-circuit to flashv2 if contiguous_kv_ratio >= 0.85; perf -> p95 192ms. still slightly worse than release but better than master.
maria: good signal. sounds like allocator fragmentation reduces contiguous_kv_ratio. we should capture contiguous_kv_ratio metric in runtime telemetry.
jon: also add batching heuristic telemetry: current batcher uses max_tokens/worker heuristic; we may need to backoff batch size when pagewalks spike. a small adaptive backoff (reduce batch_size by 25% if page_faults/sec > threshold) could avoid falling back kernels.
eva: agree. plan: 1) add contiguous_kv_ratio + page_faults telemetry, 2) add quick A/B toggle in kernel selector to enforce conservative choice, 3) test allocator variants. anyone want to own a short perf experiment?
dana: i'll run allocator variants across slab sizes [32,64,128] and hot_reserve [6,12,18] and collect p95 + contiguous_kv_ratio. ETA EOD.
kevin: i'll land the kernel-selector guard behind a feature flag (ff.paged_attn.kernel_guard) and add metric emission.
maria: thanks. if we confirm this is allocator churn -> kernel fallback, next step is either tweak alloc heuristics (coalesce free ranges) or improve kernel to better handle fragmented KV (longer copy paths but less pagewalk penalty).
sre-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: build/bench/paged_attn_regress/2419998888 (ci).
jon: awesome. one more ask: add a tiny stress test that creates frequent small allocations for KV (simulate many short prompts) so we don't regress again.
eva: noted. I'll add that to the perf harness.
maria: perfect. we'll reconvene after runs. :thumbsup:
